findings.evidence: Step 2 and Step 3 repeat the same pointers to references/resolution-stops.md#owner-stop and references/state-management.md#pinned-resume many times, and the same sentence carries restated rules such as "a pinned resume keeps the saved injection" and "rounds 1–3 reuse $INJECTION_JSON". This repetition uses tokens without adding knowledge.
findings.fix: Say each routing rule once, in a short 'Which path applies' table at the top of Step 2 (fresh, pinned resume, unpinned resume, trust-local yes, round 4+). Replace each later repeat with a one-word pointer to that table. Remove no rule, and record the merged lines in the skill's audit record.

findings.evidence: "**At the start of every fix round, in either mode, increment `$FIX_ROUND` ... (block below; new rounds only, never on a resume, a re-invoke that kept its scalars or a Step-2 re-entry, which keep the round and anchor, yet at 4 or more still take the floor below)". This follows the Process pattern, but the phase checkpoints are buried in long parenthetical prose and not laid out as a phased sequence.
findings.fix: Add a per-task checklist near the top of Step 3: Task paths → wake (first task) → resume check → resolve → gates/guard → dispatch → classify → clear resume. Then each paragraph explains one checklist item, so the Process pattern has visible checkpoints.

findings.evidence: The NEVER list is expert-grade and each item points to its step, but most reasons live in references/design-notes.md, which the skill tells the agent not to load. There is also no Gotchas section for host facts like "claude has no exec formula in the runner" or "Codex workspace-write is not an unconditional boundary". Those facts are scattered through Step 3 prose.
findings.fix: Add a short '## Gotchas' list under NEVER. Lift the existing environment facts into it: claude has no runner exec formula; Codex workspace-write writable roots vary with the owner's config; an older Node crash is a real_error, never a pair switch; pi and copilot exec are verified by self-test only. Keep the original sentences in Step 3 or point to the list from there.

findings.evidence: The description says "Runs a superpowers implementation plan ...". It is declarative rather than imperative and lacks some user-intent keywords such as 'model per task', 'quota' and 'Codex/opencode lane'.
findings.fix: Runs a superpowers implementation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/*.md) under superpowers:subagent-driven-development, choosing a live-quota-checked (runtime, model) pair for each task's implementer: native subagent or external CLI such as Codex, opencode or pi. It handles quota waits and rounds 4-5 escalation, starts the plan's unit branch before the first task, and folds, pushes and readies it after the final review through ai-kit-commit-fold. Use this when ai-kit-spec-execute detects a superpowers plan, or when asked to run or execute a superpowers plan with subagents, pick a model or lane per task, or continue or resume such a run, even without the word 'injection'. Not for superpowers:executing-plans (inline, no dispatch point), for writing or reviewing a plan, or for folding a branch on its own (ai-kit-commit-fold).

findings.evidence: SKILL.md is 291 lines, with ten references gated by MANDATORY or Do-NOT-Load triggers. But references/resolution-stops.md#owner-stop is required from more than eight places, and Step 3 still inlines long native-branch, session-fallback and exec-confinement paragraphs (lines 209-277) that apply only to some modes.
findings.fix: Move the native-branch details into a gated reference, read only when mode is native: the host-config audit commands, the Agent model and resume rules, and the session-fallback paragraph. Also move the exec-confinement paragraph into references/dispatch-external-cli.md, which already loads only for external_cli. Leave a one-line trigger at each spot.

findings.evidence: "A task that must commit checks the lane's effective policy there and in the owner's codex configuration first; when Git metadata is read-only, stop for the owner". This is a fragile, high-consequence check given only as prose, while the rest of the skill gives exact bash blocks.
findings.fix: Give the exact check as a command, for example: test that `git -C "$CWD" rev-parse --git-dir` is writable under the lane's sandbox, or read the effective writable roots from the codex config. That matches the exact-block calibration the skill uses elsewhere for the fragile steps.

findings.evidence: Output evals: 18 cases, realistic, with fixture configs and verifiable assertions. Script tests: tests/test_ai_kit_spec_superpowers.py (182 tests) plus many text tests; the shim has --help. Trigger queries: 22, with only 10 positives and 12 negatives, and the positives are almost all explicit 'superpowers plan ... subagent-driven-development' phrasings. Missing: implicit positives (no 'superpowers' word) and a resume/continue phrasing. Several evals (precise-config-active-never-asks, edge-spec-config-missing-stops) carry only 2 assertions.
findings.fix: Add 2-3 should-trigger queries where the connection is implicit, for example 'continue the plan run that stopped on codex quota yesterday, task 3' or 'run docs/superpowers/plans/x.md, use a cheaper model for the easy tasks'. Drop one weak negative to keep about 20 queries. Give each 2-assertion eval a third assertion that checks a concrete scalar or file outcome.

findings.evidence: Line 209 says session fallback "keeps the rounds 4–5 rule below, then dispatches through the native branch". Line 216 says "when the task's injection carries the session fallback, rounds 4–5 run on the session model with no ladder escalation and no model bump". Following the session-fallback branch at FIX_ROUND=4: one line says to apply the rounds 4–5 rule, and the other says no escalation applies. The reader has to guess which wins.
findings.fix: Rewrite line 209 to say: 'at rounds 4–5 it runs on the session model with no ladder escalation and no model bump (see the rounds 4–5 paragraph)'. That way both sentences state the same outcome.

findings.evidence: The re-entry conditions for Step 2 and Step 3 are spread across lines 152, 205-207 and 216-217 in nested parentheticals: pinned vs unpinned resume, restored FIX_ROUND >= 4, trust-local yes, and a new round vs a re-invoke. Following the 'unpinned resume at restored round 4' branch needs four cross-checks across paragraphs. Otherwise it is usable, with exact blocks and owner-stop fallbacks.
findings.fix: Add a decision table at the start of Step 2: rows for fresh task, pinned resume, unpinned resume at round 0-3, unpinned resume at round 4+, trust-local yes, and new fix round 1-3 or 4-5. Columns: run Step 2 resolve?, increment FIX_ROUND?, load escalation.md?, dispatch path. Point the existing prose at the table.

findings.evidence: The Codex sandbox evidence line cites https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security but no date checked. Facts not verified online.
findings.fix: Add the date checked to the Evidence line, for example '(checked 2026-11-26)'.
